title: Hook manifest
description: ONE harness hook for ONE event: scripts `<id>.sh` and/or `<id>.ps1` next to this manifest, run by the client on that event once the user consented to them, and the fallback `<id>.md`, the directive a client that runs no hooks reads instead. A script that reacts to several events ships as several hooks, so each wiring has its own consent hash.

event.description: The neutral event the hook runs on, mapped to each client's own name by fluxor-sync (`EVENTS` in tools/fluxor_sync.py): sessionStart, promptSubmit, preTool, postTool, postToolFailure (a tool call that failed or was interrupted: Claude Code only), stop, notification; or statusLine, which Claude Code draws from the script's output.

tools.description: preTool, postTool and postToolFailure only: the tools the hook runs for. `any` (the default) or the neutral families, which fluxor-sync maps to each client's tool names.

notifications.description: notification only: the notifications the hook runs for. None listed means every one.

timeoutMs.description: How long the client lets the script run before it stops it.

sends.description: What the hook sends off the machine and where, shown to the user before they consent; null when it sends nothing. Required, so a hook that sends data cannot leave it unsaid.

to.description: The host or base URL it sends to; it may be a `{{PARAM}}` the project sets.

what.description: Each piece of data that leaves the machine, in plain words.
